items.title: Microsoft releases Windows OOB updates to distrust eMudhra certificates
items.description: Microsoft has released out-of-band (OOB) Windows updates to remove trust in certificates tied to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys, protecting systems that do not receive automatic certificate trust updates. [...]

items.title: Beware the Slasher: AI Could Kill Off Cybersecurity Pros' Skills
items.description: Nathan Hamiel outlines potential SecOps horror in the AI midst, as core technical capabilities go the way of reading an atlas or remembering phone numbers.

items.title: Warp discloses breach exposing AI agent logs, user telemetry data

items.description: Attackers are increasingly abusing legitimate IT tools, Microsoft 365 sessions, and everyday workflows to compromise businesses without triggering traditional defenses. items.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
items.description: The GoAhead embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list into its default TLS backend but never turned revocation checking on, so a revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups. items.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
items.description: Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file. items.title: HPE Patches Dozens of Critical Flaws in Networking Products

items.title: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
items.description: An attacker who gained access to Keystone's website obtained the key that its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, the company said in a statement on October 26. Someone with that key could build counterfeit devices that pass the online check owners use to verify a Keystone. items.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
items.description: Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing. Attackers can recreate familiar login screens, impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations. Some fake login pages go beyond stealing passwords. items.title: So Many AI Security Benchmarks, But None Tell the Whole Story
